title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
Deepfake pornographic videos featuring the faces of Dutch public figures were created and distributed on a platform with millions of monthly visitors. The system that enabled this deployment—a platform that pays users for viral uploads and shields them with anonymity—removed human judgment about what content should be permitted. The videos constitute sexual abuse material under law, yet the platform's design made enforcement of those laws difficult for victims and authorities.

What enabled the harm was not a model making false predictions, but a social platform deployed without effective human review of uploaded content. The platform's financial incentive structure and anonymity features created conditions where the system could be used to produce and spread non-consensual intimate imagery at scale. It is not established whether the platform operators knew the videos were being created, though legal experts warned that without intervention more would appear.

The incident shows that AI-generated sexual abuse material can be deployed through existing platforms without specialized detection. It required multiple victims filing criminal complaints and members of parliament proposing intervention before any response was documented. A system designed to verify consent before uploading intimate imagery, human review of flagged content, or platform policies against deepfake pornography would have caught this in advance.

summary:
Multiple Dutch celebrities are considering legal action after discovering manipulated pornographic videos featuring their faces. These deepfake videos appear on an online platform with 13 million monthly visitors and include numerous Dutch entertainers, television presenters, Olympic athletes, government officials, mayors, and members of the royal family. Several victims have already filed reports with authorities, while others are exploring legal options. Acting Justice Minister Yesilgöz called the videos disturbing and urged victims to press charges.

Deepfake pornography involves digitally placing a person's head onto an adult video performer. The platform allegedly pays users who upload viral content and encourages anonymity to avoid prosecution. Legal experts warn that without government intervention, more fake videos will emerge. Deepfake pornography falls under revenge porn laws and is criminal. Victims can file reports, attempt to shut down websites through prosecutors, start class action lawsuits, file complaints with data protection authorities, or contact hosting companies. Previously, presenter Welmoed Sijtsma pursued the person who created deepfake videos of her, resulting in a 39-year-old Amersfoort man receiving a conditional sentence of 180 hours in November.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
